# dsh-backup — DeepSeek Harness backup & migration kit

A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) **skill** that packages your
DSH plugins, profiles, plugin settings and cha

t data into a single, restorable migration kit — so a broken
machine (or a brand-new one) can be tur
ned into a copy of the current setup.
Everything is plain PowerShell 5.1 + 7-Zip-free `tar`, no build step, no node dependency.
## What it does
`make-kit.ps1` produces one `.zip` containing:
| Path in zip | Content |
| `installer/` | the **same-version DSH desktop installer** (from the electron-updater cache), so th

e target machine runs an identical build |
| `backup/config/` | `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh` config: `profil
es/{desktop,web}` (`package.json`, `cordis.patch.yml`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`), settings, plugin config, `

dsh-claude-style`-style per-plugin data |
| `backup/offline/profiles/*/node_modules/` | the full off

line plugin `node_modules` (hoisted, symlink-free), so plugins work without network |
| `backup/user

-data-optional/` | chat history `sessions/` and `attachments/` (opt-out) |
| `backup/scripts/` | res

tore / verify / repair scripts |
| `manifest.json` + `kit-manifest.json` | per-file SHA-256 manifest
and kit metadata (version, installer hash, signature check) |
`restore-dsh.ps1` on the new machine:

1. checks the target DSH is **not running**, and records running process IDs as a baseline;
2. renam

es the existing `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh` to `.dsh.bak-<timestamp>` (rollback point);
3. copies the backe

d-up config;
4. compares `profiles\*\package.json` with the backup (detects a DSH that was launched

every declared dependency resolves** — no fake success;
6. **rewrites `.modules.yaml`** `storeDir` /

`virtualStoreDir` to the local pnpm paths (otherwise pnpm fails
with `ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_STORE` on

a different machine);
7. restores `sessions/` + `attachments/` by default, then recreates missing w
fig`, then optionally relaunches DSH.
If anything is still off after a restore, `fix-restored-dsh.ps1` trims the repair: it re-copies plug

in
`node_modules`, rewrites `.modules.yaml`, restores sessions/attachments and recreates workspace f
e_modules`, rewrites `.modules.yaml`, restores sessions/attachments and recreates workspace folders.
## Requirements

- Windows 10/11, Windows PowerShell 5.1 (bundled) — no extra runtime;
- DSH **desktop** app installe

d (the skill drives the desktop profile);
- the same-version DSH installer for the target machine: f

ound automatically in
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\@deepseek-aidsh-desktop-updater\installer.exe` (written by DSH

(including the tray icon). Plugins and config files are
rewritten by a running app.

DSH discovers it on the next launch (`Settings → Skills` should list **dsh-backup**). You can also c

opy the
folder manually — a skill is just a directory with `SKILL.md`.
## Usage
**Backup (inside DSH chat).** Ask the assistant:
> 备份当前 DSH 配置，生成迁移包

The skill runs `scripts\make-kit.ps1`, which writes
`%USERPROFILE%\Desktop\DSH备份\zips\DSH-migration-

kit-<dsh-version>-<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>.zip` plus a `.sha256`
sidecar, and prunes older kits (keep the n
ewest one by default).
**Backup (standalone PowerShell).**
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**Restore on another machine.**
1. Install the **same DSH version** from `installer/` in the zip; launch once, then quit (tray → Exi

t).
2. Extract the zip, then run:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

(or `restore-dsh.ps1` directly; `-DryRun` previews the plan)
3. Do **not** launch DSH while the rest

ore is running — the script aborts if it detects a new DSH process.
4. After the restore: check the

plugin list and open an old conversation. Then log in again and re-enter any
third-party provider AP

I key (the kit deliberately contains **no credentials**).
5. If plugins show "package unavailable" o

r old sessions fail to open:
`backup\scripts\fix-restored-dsh.ps1 -RestartApp`.

## Safety & privacy notes
- The kit contains **your personal chat history and attachments** by default. Treat the zip as priva

te; use
`-SkipUserData` to exclude them.
- No credentials, API keys or `.credentials.yaml` are ever

included.
- The restore script **moves** `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh` to `.dsh.bak-<timestamp>`; delete that

folder after you
have verified the restore.
- Project source code / workspaces are **not** included

— only the config knows their paths; the restore
script recreates missing workspace folders as empt

y directories.
- This is a community project, not an official DeepSeek tool. Test on a disposable ma

s.
- This is a community project, not an official DeepSeek tool. Test on a disposable machine first.
